classification.difficultyReason: Track signed turns through self-intersecting paths and use the scaffolded walking interpretation to explain the convex-polygon exterior-angle sum.

content.prompt: In Exercise 7B, you proved that the sum of the exterior angles of a convex polygon is $360^\circ$. This question introduces another way of looking at this theorem.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In each diagram below, imagine that you started at the point $X$, facing $A$, and walked around the figure back to $X$, passing through the vertices $A$, $B$, $C$, … in alphabetical order. Through how many complete revolutions would you turn during your journey? Count clockwise rotation as negative, and anticlockwise revolutions as positive.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with X on CA and an initial travel arrow towards A. Ordinary source blue outlines become black; the starting point and travel direction retain distinct standard accents.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; no turning result shown.

answer.worked: The turns at $A$, $B$ and $C$ are all anticlockwise and together make one complete turn. The total signed turn is $+360^\circ$, so the journey gives $+1$ revolution.

spec.description: Convex pentagon ABCDE with X on EA and a travel arrow towards A; all five vertices and the starting point remain labelled.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; no turning result shown.

answer.worked: Every vertex produces a clockwise turn. Together these turns make one complete clockwise revolution: a signed turn of $-360^\circ$, or $-1$ revolution.

spec.description: Crossed quadrilateral ABCD with BC crossing DA, no vertex or dot at the crossing, and X on DA below the crossing.
spec.mathematics: Traverse X–A–B–C–D–X. Oppositely oriented loops give cancelling signed turns.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; no turning result shown.

answer.worked: The anticlockwise turns at $A$ and $B$ are cancelled by the clockwise turns at $C$ and $D$. Continue straight through the crossing each time; it is not a vertex. The net signed turn is $0^\circ$, giving $0$ revolutions.

spec.description: Eight-vertex crossed path ABCDEFGH with a small interior triangular loop, EF crossing GH without a vertex, and X on HA pointing towards A.
spec.mathematics: The outer circuit and small loop have anticlockwise winding; total signed turning is two revolutions.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; no turning result shown.

answer.worked: Following the vertices in order produces an anticlockwise turn at every vertex. The outer circuit and the small interior loop together give two complete anticlockwise turns. Continue straight through the crossing. The total signed turn is $+720^\circ$, or $+2$ revolutions.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use these ideas to develop a proof that the sum of the exterior angles of a convex polygon is $360^\circ$.

answer.short: Walking once around a convex polygon turns you through one complete revolution. Each turn is an exterior angle, so their sum is $360^\circ$.
answer.worked: Walk anticlockwise once around the boundary of a convex polygon. At each vertex, the change in direction is the exterior angle there. Convexity means every turn is anticlockwise. Over one circuit, your direction makes exactly one complete revolution and returns to its starting direction. Therefore the sum of the exterior angles is $360^\circ$.
